AFWD.justification: The forward movement up the hierarchy toward higher complexity classes

AREV.justification: The reduction of a complex set to its simpler constituent Borel components

CLINK.justification: The sequential application of unions and intersections defining the Borel set

ENGAGR.justification: The exact rank where the set is simultaneously at the limit of collapse and persistence

EVALF.justification: The state where the density remains strictly above the collapse threshold

EVALT.justification: The state where the density of the sum-free complement reaches the threshold limit

FFUSE.justification: The merging of partitioned density estimates back into a single gap value

FSPLIT.justification: The bifurcation of the complement into potential sum-free and non-sum-free components

IFIX.justification: The permanent numerical value assigned to the threshold of collapse

IMSCRIB.justification: The invariant condition where no two elements sum to a third element within the set

TANCH.justification: The final boundary where the gap collapse is fully characterized and bounded

VINIT.justification: The initial state before any subset selection or Borel classification occurs

steps.domain_action: Initialize the universe of natural number subsets
Construct the complement set within the Borel hierarchy
Ascend from finite sets to G-delta sets
Branch the analysis into density-vanishing and density-preserving paths
Observe the gap persistence at low Borel ranks
Re-examine the intersection properties of the complement
Increase the Borel rank toward the threshold
Reach the critical rank where collapse and persistence coexist
Confirm the collapse of the gap at the threshold rank
Recombine the density components to verify the total measure
Record the specific Borel rank as the collapse constant
Seal the classification within the descriptive set theory domain
